transcript.text: Alright, everyone's here, so let's get started. I've been asked to make a costume for a small neighborhood theater production. Before I decide whether to take on the commission, I want to go over the terms together. Marco, Tess, Hugo — does each of you have any offer, constraint, or production requirement I should know about? Let's hear it one by one so I can get the full picture before I make my decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: My proposal is eight one-hour pottery lessons plus $60 in cash in exchange for an 18th-century black waistcoat, with a fitting on June 3 at 18:00 and delivery on June 15 at 18:00.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'm ready to pay Lina exactly $480 in cash for a different costume commission of similar sewing complexity, with no barter involved.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: The theater's stage manager told me that this waistcoat must use flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric and include a reflective trim strip exactly 50 millimeters wide. I haven't shared that with anyone until now.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Accept Marco's offer of 8 one-hour pottery lessons plus $60 cash for an 18th-century black waistcoat, with fitting on June 3 at 18:00 and delivery on June 15 at 18:00.
The waistcoat must use flame-resistant black wool-blend fabric with a reflective trim strip exactly 50mm wide, as required by the theater's stage manager.
Tess's $480 cash offer for a similar-complexity costume is noted as a benchmark. Marco's offer is accepted instead as the neighborhood theater commission.
